records.region: La Guajira, Colombia; selected Ranchería receiving-corridor setting
records.candidate_name_role: Partially supported representative receiving-system identity; whole-feature completion withheld
records.material_pending_reason: Río Ranchería is supported as a candidate for the receiving middle corridor. The selected opening, upstream connection, lower branch choices and final coastal passage remain unresolved. No name is accepted or automatically applied.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Bounded representative receiving-river candidate for the supported middle corridor. The opening, entry relationship, selected lower branches and actual coastal terminal remain unresolved. This is not a name for every selected reach.
records.completion_scope: One primary material-pending status. The independent original supports a bounded named receiving corridor, but the required full geographic correspondence is incomplete. This is not a completed scope hold. Research stopped after the planned single independent map publication, preserving actual gaps instead of expanding source acquisition.
records.supported_name_scope: Bounded representative receiving-river candidate for the supported middle corridor. The opening, entry relationship, selected lower branches and actual coastal terminal remain unresolved. This is not a name for every selected reach.

scope_limits: The headward opening and upper-to-receiving through-link are material gaps.
Middle-corridor representative identity does not certify every selected part or impose a uniform river name.
The exact selected lower-branch route and actual terminal passage remain unresolved despite regional downstream context.
No source supports an assertion that the entire selection is presently a continuously flowing natural channel.
The published date is not evidence of present shoreline position or current infrastructure operation.

records.region: Northeast Greenland, Inland Ice and exposed-rock margins around southern and eastern Dronning Louise Land, approaching the southern Storstrømmen regional setting and southwestern Dove Bugt.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Dronning Louise Land, Storstrømmen and Dove Bugt are geographic context labels, not candidates for the whole modeled river group.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The retained original covers the complete selected geography but establishes neither a representative named natural river nor continuous surveyed surface or subglacial flow across this modeled ice-and-rock sequence. Contextual land, ice and bay labels cannot name the whole river group.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection opens in mapped inland ice south of Dronning Louise Land, first runs briefly south and then east/northeast, crosses the generalized southern and eastern ice/exposed-rock corridor, and ends after a northward lower-ice approach at the southwestern Dove Bugt ice/coastal-water setting. No exact glacier assignment or natural-river identity is inferred from this terrain sequence.
records.completion_scope: All 57 selected parts and their joins were inspected against contiguous pixels of the actual retained national original, with clean opening, full-corridor and terminal views plus original graticules, projection, legend and imprint. No substantial selected geographic interval remains unviewed at ordinary source scale. Approximate map orientation is not exact bank, vertex or modern glacier-front matching.

component_scope_limits: Dronning Louise Land identifies regional exposed-land geography. Storstrømmen is a contextual ice label; no precise selected glacier or river reach is assigned. Dove Bugt identifies adjacent coastal water. None names the modeled river group.

The original legend distinguishes ice surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments. Their intersections with the selected line do not establish flowing water.
No selected continuous lake-throughflow, lake-outlet connection, reservoir or managed-channel connector is established.

Historical geological and glaciological cartography supports generalized terrain and terminal setting, not exact contemporary glacier-front position, ordinary river-mouth location or present hydraulic behavior.
A null candidate means this source pass did not establish a name; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.region: Southern California, United States; selected Cienaga Seca Creek and Santa Ana River corridor
records.material_pending_reason: The selected transfer from Santa Ana River across East Highland pond/excavation terrain to Plunge Creek is not established by the corridor or higher-detail original. Separate mapped tributaries and their downstream confluence do not establish this earlier through-link. The short selected hillside opening above Little Cienaga is not fully established as a channel approach to Cienaga Seca Creek. The named valley downstream is mapped.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Santa Ana River is the supported receiving-river and downstream corridor identity. Cienaga Seca Creek is a distinct selected headward reach, and the maps distinguish Plunge Creek and Chino Creek in intermediate settings. A completed representative identity for the whole selected object is withheld because a selected cross-link is not established.
records.completion_scope: Five bounded original USGSTopo views identify the selected Cienaga Seca Creek and Santa Ana River corridors, the mountain-canyon dam passage, the Prado flood-control basin and dam passage, the lower urban river, and its Pacific coastal outlet. They also distinguish Santa Ana River from Plunge Creek around East Highland. The selected northern detour crosses the intervening pond/excavation terrain without an established mapped through-channel. This is a material correspondence gap, not an access failure or a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Santa Ana River is the supported receiving-river and downstream corridor identity. Cienaga Seca Creek is a distinct selected headward reach, and the maps distinguish Plunge Creek and Chino Creek in intermediate settings. A completed representative identity for the whole selected object is withheld because a selected cross-link is not established.

scope_limits: The two specified selected through-approaches remain unresolved. A familiar receiving-river name and a mapped downstream confluence cannot replace evidence for them.
The finding does not impose Santa Ana River as a scalar name on the distinct Cienaga Seca Creek approach, Plunge Creek setting, managed basin or all selected parts.
The source is composite cartography, not a present-day survey of bank position, shoreline, water levels, channel activation, dam releases or pond operations.
Formal hydronym boundaries, legal naming status and Korean name selection were not verified.

records.region: Western Alaska; selected southeastern feeder, South Fork Buckland River, Buckland River and branching lower river north of Buckland settlement.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The southeastern selected approach is an unnamed feeder entering South Fork Buckland River; the separate Middle, North and West Forks are incoming mapped branches. Their junctions and the repeatedly labeled Buckland River support a representative system candidate without forcing a common name onto each part. The actual modeled terminal remains inside the lower-river branching network, so a familiar downstream sea or bay name is not substituted for its observed location.
records.completion_scope: All 49 parts of the single selected mainstem fragment are covered by three overlapping, readable original USGSTopo views. The chosen southeastern opening, northward and westward feeder bend, South Fork join, fork-junction area, middle Buckland River meanders, West Fork junction, western/northern bend, continuation past Buckland settlement and actual branching lower-river endpoint have ordinary corridor-scale correspondence. No material geographic through-link remains unviewed or unsupported at this bounded scale. Generalized model offsets and clipped meanders are not interpreted as exact-bank correspondence.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected selected system, supported by the named receiving Buckland River and connected South Fork approach. The initial unnamed feeder and South Fork are not assigned one uniform Buckland River scalar name. The actual selected endpoint is within the lower river, rather than an established marine mouth.

naming_scope_details.actual_terminal_setting: Broad branching lower Buckland River north of Buckland settlement; mapped channels continue downstream.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
